sources.entry: superpowers — Tooling for giving AI systems richer capabilities and more flexible action patterns in practical workflows.

Superpowers by Jesse Vincent - A strong bundle of core competencies for software engineering, with good coverage of a large portion of the SDLC - from planning, reviewing, testing, debugging... Well written, well organized, and adaptable. The author refers to them as "superpowers", but many of them are just consolidating engineering best practices - which sometimes does feel like a superpower when

summary.one_liner: Superpowers is a software development methodology and skills library for coding agents that enforces a structured workflow of brainstorming, planning, test-driven development, subagent execution, and code review.
keywords: help ai agent write better code
summary.what_it_does: Superpowers is a set of composable skills plus bootstrap instructions that make a coding agent follow a defined development process. When the agent detects a building task, it asks clarifying questions, presents a design in short chunks for approval, and then writes an implementation plan with small tasks, exact file paths, and verification steps. Execution can run through subagent-driven development with a review after each task, or inline via executing-plans with one final review. The library includes skills for test-driven development, systematic debugging, verification before completion, requesting and receiving code review, git worktrees, finishing a branch, dispatching parallel agents, and writing new skills. A diagnosing-superpowers skill reviews session transcripts to explain misbehavior. The README says skills trigger automatically and that it can work autonomously for a couple of hours on an approved plan.
use_cases: enforce test-first development with a coding agent
plan a feature before an AI agent writes code
run a multi-task implementation with reviewed subagents
debug a bug systematically with an agent
isolate feature work on a separate git branch
review agent-written code against a plan
investigate why an agent session went wrong
how_to_run: In Claude Code, run: /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official
Or add the marketplace: /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace, then /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
Codex CLI: open /plugins, search for superpowers, select Install Plugin
Gemini CLI: gemini extensions install <repo URL from README>
Install separately for each coding agent harness you use; start a new session after installing
stack: Plugin or extension packages for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code, Hermes Agent, Muse, Antigravity, Devin CLI, Factory Droid, Kimi Code, Grok Build CLI
Drill eval harness (superpowers-evals) for skill-behavior tests
npm test and run-*.sh scripts for plugin infrastructure tests
notable: Skills trigger automatically, so the user does not need to invoke them manually
Two review modes: subagent-driven development with per-task review, or executing-plans with one final review
Plans are written for a reader with no project context, emphasizing RED-GREEN-REFACTOR, YAGNI, and DRY
diagnosing-superpowers skill reads session transcripts and can export a scrubbed bundle for a bug report
Broad harness support, with a separate install step for each agent
caveats: The README says new skill contributions are generally not accepted, and updates must work across all supported agents
Install is per harness; a user with several agents must install separately for each
Optional visual companion sends a logo request to the author's website with the version number; it can be disabled with SUPERPOWERS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY
Hermes loses the bootstrap after compaction in very long sessions, per the README
